title: Indian Constitutional Amendments - UGC NET Law Question Bank
note: Covers Amendments up to the 106th (2023). Verify any Amendment enacted after that date.

questions.question: Which of the following requires a special majority AND ratification by at least half of the State legislatures under Art. 368(2)?

options.B: Formation of new States under Art. 3

questions.explanation: Arts. 2, 3, 4, Fifth and Sixth Schedules and citizenship can be changed by simple majority outside Art. 368. Election of the President is in the proviso to Art. 368(2) requiring State ratification.

questions.question: Shankari Prasad Singh Deo v. Union of India (1951) upheld the validity of which Amendment?
questions.explanation: Held that the power to amend under Art. 368 includes power to amend Fundamental Rights; 'law' in Art. 13 does not include constitutional amendments.

questions.question: Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan (1965) concerned the validity of which Amendment?
questions.explanation: Upheld the 17th Amendment (1964) following Shankari Prasad, though two judges (Hidayatullah, Mudholkar) expressed doubts on basic features.

questions.question: I.C. Golak Nath v. State of Punjab (1967) was decided by a bench of:

options.A: 7 judges, unanimously, upholding the Ninth Schedule
options.B: 13 judges, by 7:6, propounding the basic structure doctrine
options.C: 11 judges, by 6:5, holding Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights
options.D: 9 judges, by 5:4, upholding Parliament's power to amend Fundamental Rights

questions.explanation: Golak Nath overruled Shankari Prasad and Sajjan Singh, applying the doctrine of prospective overruling.

questions.question: Which Amendment was enacted to nullify the effect of Golak Nath and inserted Art. 13(4) and Art. 368(3)?
questions.explanation: 24th Amendment declared Parliament's power to amend any provision incl. Part III, made Presidential assent compulsory and amended the marginal note of Art. 368.

questions.question: Article 31C (Directive Principles in Art. 39(b) and (c) to prevail over Arts. 14, 19 and 31) was inserted by:
questions.explanation: 25th Amendment also replaced 'compensation' by 'amount' in Art. 31(2).

questions.question: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) was decided by a bench of ____ judges with a majority of ____.
questions.explanation: The Court held Parliament can amend any provision but not alter the 'basic structure'. It struck down the 2nd part of Art. 31C (excluding judicial review) inserted by the 25th Amendment.

questions.question: Which provisions inserted by the 42nd Amendment were struck down in Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)?
questions.explanation: Minerva Mills held limited amending power is itself a basic feature and that harmony between Part III and Part IV is part of the basic structure; it also struck down the extended Art. 31C.

questions.question: In Waman Rao v. Union of India (1981), the Supreme Court fixed which date for testing Ninth Schedule laws against the basic structure?
questions.explanation: Ninth Schedule laws inserted before 24 April 1973 (the date of Kesavananda) were saved; those after are open to review. Reaffirmed in I.R. Coelho (2007).

questions.question: In I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007), a nine-judge bench held that:

options.A: Ninth Schedule laws enjoy absolute immunity
options.B: Art. 31A is a basic feature that cannot be amended
options.D: Ninth Schedule laws enacted after 24 April 1973 are open to judicial review on the touchstone of the basic structure

questions.explanation: Art. 31B immunity is not absolute; laws violating basic structure/Art. 21 and Art. 14 can be struck down.

questions.question:
I. The 24th Amendment made it obligatory for the President to give assent to Constitution Amendment Bills.
II. Art. 368(3) declares that Art. 13 shall not apply to amendments made under Art. 368.

options.A: Both I and II are correct
options.D: Neither I nor II is correct

questions.explanation: Both true. 24th Amendment (1971) inserted Art. 13(4) and 368(3) and made Presidential assent compulsory.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Judicial review of constitutional amendments is possible in India.
Reason (R): Kesavananda Bharati held that amendments violating the basic structure are void.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Basic structure review is the judicial check on Art. 368 power.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Art. 368(4) and (5) were struck down in Minerva Mills.
Reason (R): The Court held that a limited amending power is itself a basic feature of the Constitution.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Parliament cannot enlarge its own amending power into absolute power.

questions.question: The Ninth Schedule was added to the Constitution by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: Along with Arts. 31A and 31B, to protect land reform laws from judicial challenge.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT done by the First Amendment Act, 1951?

options.A: Added 'public order', 'friendly relations with foreign States' and 'incitement to an offence' as grounds under Art. 19(2)
options.D: Inserted Art. 15(4) for socially and educationally backward classes

questions.explanation: Art. 21A was inserted by the 86th Amendment (2002).

questions.question: The First Amendment inserting Art. 15(4) was a response to the decision in:

options.A: Bela Banerjee v. State of W.B.
options.B: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
options.C: State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951)

questions.explanation: The Court struck down communal G.O. for college admissions; the 1st Amendment enabled special provisions for backward classes.

questions.question: The restriction on freedom of speech in the First Amendment was a reaction to which pair of 1950 cases?

options.D: Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras and Brij Bhushan v. State of Delhi

questions.explanation: Both cases struck down press-related restrictions on grounds of 'public safety' as unconstitutional.

questions.question: The Fourth Amendment (1955) made which change to Art. 31(2)?

options.A: Adequacy of compensation was made non-justiciable
options.D: Right to property was made a legal right under Art. 300A

questions.explanation: Response to State of West Bengal v. Bela Banerjee (1954), which required 'just equivalent' compensation.

questions.question: The Seventh Amendment (1956) is associated with:

options.A: Reorganisation of States and abolition of the Part A, B, C classification

questions.explanation: It reorganised into 14 States and 6 Union Territories, enabled a common High Court for two or more States (Art. 231) and inserted Arts. 350A-350B.

questions.question: Article 350A (instruction in mother tongue at primary stage) and Art. 350B (Special Officer for linguistic minorities) were inserted by:
questions.explanation: Linked to the States Reorganisation Commission recommendations.

questions.question: The Ninth Amendment (1960) was enacted following the opinion in:

options.B: Re Berubari Union and Exchange of Enclaves (1960)

questions.explanation: The Court held cession of Indian territory requires a constitutional amendment under Art. 368, and that the Preamble is not part of the Constitution (later overruled in Kesavananda).

questions.question: Which of the following was held in Re Berubari Union (1960), later overruled?

options.C: The Preamble is a part of the basic structure
options.D: The Preamble is not a part of the Constitution

questions.explanation: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held the Preamble is part of the Constitution; Union of India v. LIC (1995) reaffirmed.

questions.question: Dadra and Nagar Haveli were incorporated into India as a Union Territory by:
questions.explanation: 12th (1962) integrated Goa, Daman and Diu; 14th (1962) integrated Puducherry.

questions.question: Special provisions for Nagaland (Art. 371A) were inserted by:
questions.explanation: Nagaland became the 16th State in 1963.

questions.question: The Fourteenth Amendment (1962) is associated with:

options.D: Incorporation of Puducherry and insertion of Art. 239A

questions.explanation: Art. 239A provides for legislatures/councils for some Union Territories.

questions.question: Which Amendment raised the retirement age of High Court judges from 60 to 62 and extended HC writ jurisdiction under Art. 226?
questions.explanation: Also permitted High Courts to issue writs to persons/authorities outside territorial limits if the cause of action arose within.

questions.question: Which Amendment inserted 'sovereignty and integrity of India' in the oath/affirmation of candidates and in Art. 19(2)-(4)?
questions.explanation: Enacted following the Sino-Indian conflict.

questions.question: Sindhi was added to the Eighth Schedule by the:
questions.explanation: 71st added Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali; 92nd added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali; 96th replaced 'Oriya' with 'Odia'. The Schedule now lists 22 languages.

questions.question: The Thirteenth Amendment is related to Nagaland, while which Amendment dealt with the creation of Meghalaya as an autonomous State within Assam?
questions.explanation: Inserted Art. 244A. 27th (1971) provided for Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh and others as Union Territories and inserted Art. 239B.

questions.question: The Seventeenth Amendment (1964) is most notable for:

options.A: Expanding the Ninth Schedule and redefining 'estate' in Art. 31A

questions.explanation: Challenged in Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan (1965).

questions.question: The Fifth Amendment (1955) amended which Article?

options.D: Article 3 (time limit for State legislatures to express views on bills affecting States)

questions.explanation: Proviso to Art. 3 enables the President to specify a period within which the State legislature may express its views.

questions.question: The Twenty-fifth Amendment replaced the word 'compensation' by 'amount' in Art. 31(2). This followed which case?

options.B: R.C. Cooper v. Union of India (Bank Nationalisation case, 1970)

questions.explanation: The Court had held that compensation must be the 'equivalent' of the property acquired.

questions.question: Abolition of Privy Purses and insertion of Art. 363A was done by:
questions.explanation: Followed Madhav Rao Scindia v. Union of India (1970-71), which struck down the Presidential Order derecognising Rulers.

questions.question: The Thirty-first Amendment (1973) increased the strength of the Lok Sabha from:
questions.explanation: Currently the maximum is 550 (530 States + 20 UTs) with the Anglo-Indian nomination ended by the 104th Amendment.

questions.question: Telangana Regional Committee and Arts. 371D and 371E were inserted by:
questions.explanation: Art. 371D relates to equitable opportunities in public employment and education in Andhra Pradesh/Telangana.

questions.question: Which Amendment removed the monetary valuation limit for civil appeals to the Supreme Court?
questions.explanation: Appeals now lie on a 'substantial question of law of general importance'.

questions.question: The Twenty-ninth Amendment (1972) placed which State land reform Acts in the Ninth Schedule?
questions.explanation: These were challenged in Kesavananda Bharati.

questions.question: Sikkim became an Associate State by the ___ Amendment and a full State by the ___ Amendment.
questions.explanation: Sikkim became the 22nd State; Art. 371F inserted. The old Tenth Schedule for Sikkim was introduced by the 35th and omitted by the 36th.

questions.question: The Thirty-third Amendment (1974) relates to:

options.A: Resignation of Members of Parliament/State Legislatures — Presiding officer must be satisfied that resignation is voluntary

questions.explanation: Amended Arts. 101(3)(b) and 190(3)(b).

questions.question: Thirty-eighth Amendment (1975) made which of the following non-justiciable?

options.D: President's satisfaction in declaring Emergency (Art. 352), and in promulgating ordinances

questions.explanation: Later reversed by the 44th Amendment.

questions.question: The Thirty-ninth Amendment (1975) placed the election of which functionaries beyond judicial scrutiny through the new Art. 329A?

options.A: President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Speaker

questions.explanation: Clause (4) of Art. 329A was struck down in Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975).

questions.question: In Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975) the Supreme Court struck down which part of the 39th Amendment?

options.A: Clause (4) of Art. 329A, as violating free and fair elections, democracy and rule of law (basic structure)

questions.explanation: The Court applied the basic structure doctrine for the first time to strike down a constitutional amendment.

questions.question: The Fortieth Amendment (1976) dealt with:

options.A: Territorial waters, continental shelf, EEZ and maritime zones (Art. 297)

questions.explanation: Also added more laws to the Ninth Schedule.

questions.question: Which Committee's recommendations led to the Forty-second Amendment (1976)?
questions.explanation: Often called a 'Mini Constitution'.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT done by the Forty-second Amendment?
questions.explanation: Art. 21A came by the 86th Amendment. The 42nd also added Arts. 39A, 43A, 48A and 31D.

questions.question: Part XIVA (Arts. 323A and 323B) on Tribunals was inserted by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997) held clauses excluding High Court jurisdiction unconstitutional.

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties were originally ____ in number, and the 11th duty was added by the ____ Amendment.
questions.explanation: Art. 51A(k): duty of parent/guardian to provide education to child aged 6-14.

questions.question: The term of Lok Sabha was extended from five to six years by the ____ Amendment and restored to five years by the ____ Amendment.
questions.explanation: The extension was to remain valid during Emergency; 44th also restored Art. 83(2) and 172(1).

questions.question: Which Amendment deleted Art. 19(1)(f) and Art. 31 and made property a legal right under Art. 300A?
questions.explanation: Property ceased to be a Fundamental Right; it is now a constitutional right and a human right (Jilubhai Nanbhai Khachar v. State of Gujarat, 1995).

questions.question: The Forty-fourth Amendment replaced 'internal disturbance' in Art. 352 with:
questions.explanation: Emergency must now be approved by Parliament within one month by special majority, and Arts. 20 and 21 cannot be suspended.

questions.question: Under the Forty-fourth Amendment, which Fundamental Rights cannot be suspended during Emergency (Art. 359)?
questions.explanation: Overcame ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla (1976) which had held Art. 21 could be suspended.

questions.question: ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla (1976) was effectively superseded by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: Habeas Corpus case; the 44th Amendment ensured that Arts. 20-21 remain enforceable during Emergency.

questions.question: The Forty-third Amendment (1977) is notable for:

options.D: Repealing Arts. 31D and 32A inserted by the 42nd Amendment, restoring judicial review powers

questions.explanation: It restored the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and High Courts curtailed by the 42nd.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The 44th Amendment removed the Right to Property from Part III.
Reason (R): It was inserted as a legal right under Art. 300A in Part XII.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Property is now a constitutional right and not a Fundamental Right.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The 42nd Amendment is often referred to as the 'Mini Constitution'.
Reason (R): It made wide-ranging changes to the Preamble, Directive Principles, Fundamental Duties and judiciary.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment undid many of its changes.

questions.question:
I. Art. 31C was inserted by the 25th Amendment and extended by the 42nd Amendment to all Directive Principles.
II. The extended Art. 31C was struck down in Minerva Mills (1980).

options.A: Both I and II are correct
options.D: Neither I nor II is correct

questions.explanation: Both true.

questions.question: The Anti-Defection Law and the Tenth Schedule were introduced by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: Arts. 101, 102, 190 and 191 were amended to include disqualification on defection.

questions.question: Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992) held that:

options.A: The Speaker's decision is final and non-justiciable
options.B: The Tenth Schedule is valid but paragraph 7 (ouster of jurisdiction) is unconstitutional for want of ratification
options.D: The entire Tenth Schedule is unconstitutional

questions.explanation: Decided by a 3:2 majority; the Speaker acts as a tribunal and his decisions are subject to judicial review.

questions.question: Which Amendment removed the exception regarding 'split' in the Tenth Schedule?
questions.explanation: Also capped the Council of Ministers at 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha (Art. 75(1A)) and inserted Art. 361B.

questions.question: The minimum voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by:
questions.explanation: Art. 326 was amended; came into force on 28 March 1989.

questions.question: Special provisions for Mizoram (Art. 371G) were inserted by the:
questions.explanation: 55th → Arunachal Pradesh (Art. 371H); 56th → Goa (Art. 371I).

questions.question: Authoritative text of the Constitution in Hindi was provided under Art. 394A inserted by the:
questions.explanation: President may publish authoritative Hindi translation.

questions.question: The Sixtieth Amendment (1988) increased the ceiling of profession tax from:
questions.explanation: Amended Art. 276(2).

questions.question: Delhi was given the status of 'National Capital Territory' by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: Inserted Arts. 239AA and 239AB. Government of NCT of Delhi v. Union of India (2018) interpreted these provisions.

questions.question: The Seventy-third Amendment (1992) added which Part and Schedule?
questions.explanation: Arts. 243 to 243-O; the Eleventh Schedule has 29 subjects.

questions.question: The Seventy-fourth Amendment (1992) inserted:

options.A: Part IXA (Municipalities) and Twelfth Schedule (18 subjects)

questions.explanation: Arts. 243-P to 243-ZG.

questions.question: Art. 243-D requires reservation of not less than ____ of total seats for women in Panchayats.
questions.explanation: Raised to one-half by several States by State legislation.

questions.question: When did the 73rd and 74th Amendments come into force respectively?
questions.explanation: Passed in December 1992 and ratified in 1993; 24 April is celebrated as National Panchayati Raj Day.

questions.question: The Seventy-second Amendment (1992) relates to:

options.B: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in Tripura Legislative Assembly

questions.explanation: Minor but frequently asked.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendments dealt with Art. 16(4A) — reservation in promotions for SC/STs?
questions.explanation: Followed Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992), which held that reservation in promotions was not permitted.

questions.question: The Seventy-sixth Amendment (1994) placed which State law in the Ninth Schedule?

options.B: Tamil Nadu Backward Classes, SC and ST (Reservation of Seats) Act, 1993 providing 69% reservation

questions.explanation: Challenged in I.R. Coelho and in the Indra Sawhney context.

questions.question: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992) was decided by a bench of:

options.B: Nine judges, upholding 27% OBC reservation but capping total reservation at 50%

questions.explanation: Also introduced the 'creamy layer' exclusion and held Art. 16(4) does not permit reservation in promotions.

questions.question: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) is related to:

options.A: Imposition of President's Rule under Art. 356 and secularism

questions.explanation: Held that Art. 356 is subject to judicial review and secularism is part of the basic structure.

questions.question: The Fifty-ninth Amendment (1988), later repealed, extended the power to impose Emergency in which State?
questions.explanation: Repealed by the 63rd Amendment (1989).

questions.question: The Sixty-fifth Amendment (1990) provided for:

options.B: National Commission for SCs and STs (Art. 338)

questions.explanation: Replaced by two separate commissions by the 89th Amendment (2003).

questions.question: The Eighty-fourth Amendment (2001) froze delimitation of constituencies until:

options.C: The first census taken after the year 2026

questions.explanation: Based on 1991 census originally; the 87th Amendment (2003) changed this to 2001 census for readjustment.

questions.question: Which Amendment shifted the base of delimitation from 1991 census to 2001 census?
questions.explanation: Delimitation was done under the Delimitation Act, 2002.

questions.question: The Eighty-fifth Amendment (2001) provided for:

options.B: Consequential seniority in promotion for SC/ST government servants (Art. 16(4A))

questions.explanation: The 81st (2000) inserted Art. 16(4B) for carry-forward vacancies; the 82nd (2000) added the proviso to Art. 335.

questions.question: M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006) upheld the validity of the 77th, 81st, 82nd and 85th Amendments subject to which conditions?

options.B: Mandatory creamy layer for SCs only
options.D: Quantifiable data on backwardness and inadequacy of representation, and maintaining administrative efficiency

questions.explanation: Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta (2018) clarified that quantifiable data on backwardness is not needed for SC/ST but creamy layer applies.

questions.question: Right to Education (Art. 21A) was inserted by the:
questions.explanation: Free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14; Right to Education Act enacted in 2009 and enforced on 1 April 2010.

questions.question: Which case recognised education as a Fundamental Right up to the age of 14 years before the 86th Amendment?

options.A: Unni Krishnan J.P. v. State of A.P. (1993)
options.B: Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka (1992)

questions.explanation: Mohini Jain (1992) first recognised right to education under Art. 21; Unni Krishnan limited it to age 14.

questions.question: The Eighty-ninth Amendment (2003) provided for:

options.A: Creation of National Commission for BCs
options.C: Division of the National Commission for SC/ST into separate commissions (Arts. 338 and 338A)

questions.explanation: Separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Art. 338A.

questions.question: Council of Ministers cannot exceed ____ of the total strength of the Lok Sabha/Legislative Assembly under the 91st Amendment.
questions.explanation: In small States, minimum 12 Ministers; Art. 164(1A).

questions.question: Service tax was brought under Art. 268A by the:
questions.explanation: Art. 268A was omitted by the 101st Amendment.

questions.question: Eightieth Amendment (2000) implemented recommendations of which Finance Commission regarding tax devolution?

options.B: Tenth Finance Commission — alternative scheme of devolution under Art. 270

questions.explanation: Altered Arts. 268-272; share of Union taxes to States.

questions.question: Ninety-fourth Amendment (2006) removed the requirement of a tribal welfare Minister in which State?
questions.explanation: Retained for Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Odisha.

questions.question: Ninety-third Amendment (2005) inserted which Clause?

options.D: Art. 15(5) — reservation in educational institutions including private unaided institutions (except minority institutions)

questions.explanation: It followed the T.M.A. Pai Foundation and Inamdar rulings on private unaided institutions.

questions.question: Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India (2008) upheld:

options.B: Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 and the 93rd Amendment, excluding the creamy layer among OBCs

questions.explanation: Constitution Bench decision by 5 judges (Justice Dalveer Bhandari dissenting in part).

questions.question: Pramati Educational & Cultural Trust v. Union of India (2014) held that Art. 15(5) is constitutionally valid:

options.B: For all private institutions including minority
options.C: Insofar as it applies to private unaided non-minority institutions; minority institutions are exempt

questions.explanation: The Court did not apply Art. 15(5) to minority institutions protected by Art. 30(1).

questions.question: Ninety-fifth Amendment (2009) extended reservation of seats for SC/ST in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies up to:
questions.explanation: Extended again by the 104th Amendment to 2030.

questions.question: Ninety-sixth Amendment (2011) replaced the word 'Oriya' in the Eighth Schedule with:
questions.explanation: Also changed the name of the State from Orissa to Odisha by a separate Act.

questions.question: Which Amendment (2011) inserted Part IXB on Co-operative Societies?
questions.explanation: Added 'co-operative societies' to Art. 19(1)(c), Art. 43B (DPSP), and Part IXB (Arts. 243ZH-243ZT).

questions.question: Special provisions for Hyderabad-Karnataka region (now Kalyana-Karnataka) are under Art. 371J, inserted by the:
questions.explanation: Provides for a regional development board and reservation in educational institutions and jobs.

questions.question: The Ninetieth Amendment (2003) relates to:

options.C: Representation of Bodoland Territorial Areas District (Art. 332(6))

questions.explanation: Retains non-tribal representation in Assam's Bodoland Territorial Council.

questions.question:
I. The 92nd Amendment added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule.
II. The 71st Amendment added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali to the Eighth Schedule.

options.A: Both I and II are correct
options.D: Neither I nor II is correct

questions.explanation: Both true. The Eighth Schedule currently has 22 languages.

questions.question: The National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) was created by the:
questions.explanation: Inserted Arts. 124A, 124B, 124C. Struck down in Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (2015) by 4:1.

questions.question: Which case is known as the 'Fourth Judges Case'?

options.B: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (2015)
options.C: In re Special Reference No. 1 of 1998
options.D: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India (1981)

questions.explanation: First Judges Case: S.P. Gupta (1981); Second: SCAORA (1993); Third: Special Reference (1998).

questions.question: The Hundredth Amendment (2015) is related to:

options.C: Land Boundary Agreement between India and Bangladesh — exchange of enclaves

questions.explanation: Altered the First Schedule (territories of Assam, West Bengal, Tripura, Meghalaya).

questions.question: The GST was introduced by the ____ Amendment, which inserted Arts. 246A, 269A and 279A.
questions.explanation: GST came into effect on 1 July 2017; the GST Council is under Art. 279A.

questions.question: The National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) was given constitutional status by the:
questions.explanation: Inserted Arts. 338B and 342A.

questions.question: The One Hundred and Fifth Amendment (2021) clarified that:

options.C: States and UTs may prepare their own lists of Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (Art. 342A(3))

questions.explanation: Overrode the effect of Jaishri Laxmanrao Patil v. Chief Minister of Maharashtra (2021) which struck down the Maratha reservation.

questions.question: Dr. Jaishri Laxmanrao Patil v. Chief Minister (2021) is also known as the:
questions.explanation: Held that after the 102nd Amendment only the President/Parliament can identify SEBCs, and that the 50% ceiling from Indra Sawhney remained intact.

questions.question: Ten percent reservation for Economically Weaker Sections was introduced by the:
questions.explanation: Inserted Arts. 15(6) and 16(6).

questions.question: In Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022), the Supreme Court upheld the 103rd Amendment by a majority of:
questions.explanation: CJI U.U. Lalit and Justice Ravindra Bhat dissented.

questions.question: Which Amendment discontinued nomination of Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies?
questions.explanation: Omitted Arts. 331 and 333 and extended SC/ST seat reservation to 2030.

questions.question: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (2023) is the ____ Amendment Act.
questions.explanation: Provides one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and Delhi Assembly (Arts. 330A, 332A, 239AA); effective after delimitation following the first census after commencement.

questions.question: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 reserves one-third of seats for women, valid for:
questions.explanation: Includes sub-reservation for SC/ST women.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The 99th Amendment creating the NJAC was declared unconstitutional.
Reason (R): It compromised the independence of the judiciary — a basic feature.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Collegium system revived in the Fourth Judges Case.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The 103rd Amendment, providing EWS reservation, was upheld by the Supreme Court.
Reason (R): The 50% ceiling is part of the basic structure and cannot be exceeded under any circumstances.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: The majority held the 50% ceiling is not inviolable and EWS reservation does not violate basic structure; hence R is false.

questions.question:
I. The 101st Amendment introduced Art. 279A (GST Council).
II. Art. 268A (service tax) was omitted by the 101st Amendment.

options.A: Both I and II are correct
options.D: Neither I nor II is correct

questions.explanation: Both true.

questions.question: Which Amendment first extended reservation for SC/ST in legislatures (originally to 1960) up to 1970?
The Seventy-ninth Amendment (1999) extended reservation for SC/ST in legislatures up to:
questions.explanation: Subsequent extensions: 95th (2020) and 104th (2030).

questions.question: Which Amendment inserted Art. 16(4B) (carry-forward of unfilled vacancies for SC/ST)?

questions.question: Which of these cases led to the First Amendment's insertion of Art. 31B and the Ninth Schedule?

questions.explanation: The Patna HC struck down the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950 as violating Art. 14; the 1st Amendment protected zamindari abolition laws.

questions.question: Which Amendment first altered Art. 3 by adding an Explanation that 'State' includes Union Territory in clause (a) of Art. 3?

questions.question: Which Amendment inserted Art. 239AA, 239AB for Delhi?
questions.explanation: Delhi has a Legislative Assembly and Council of Ministers headed by a Chief Minister.

questions.question: The Ninth Schedule's purpose is to:

questions.explanation: Art. 31B; subject to I.R. Coelho (2007).

questions.question: Which Article was inserted by the 99th Amendment as 'Judicial Appointments Commission'?
questions.explanation: Arts. 124A-124C.
